title: Empirical Bayes Selection for Value Maximization

problem.claim: Select the best m units from n using noisy, heteroskedastic measurements to maximize the aggregate true value of the selected units as m/n approaches a value in (0,1).

contributions.claim: An empirical Bayes decision rule achieves Op(n^-1) regret relative to the Bayesian oracle when the prior is parametric.
When the estimated prior has error Op(rn), the resulting regret is Op(rn2).
Using priors calibrated from more than four thousand internet experiments, empirical Bayes methods perform well at detecting the best treatments with a modest number of experiments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: An example attains the parametric regret bound.
Priors calibrated from a dataset of over four thousand internet experiments indicate good empirical performance with only a modest number of experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies value-maximizing selection under noisy, heteroskedastic measurements.
For a parametric prior, the empirical Bayes rule has Op(n^-1) regret relative to the Bayesian oracle.
More generally, prior-estimation error of Op(rn) produces regret Op(rn2).
Selection is characterized as fundamentally easier than estimating unit values.
The bound is shown to be sharp theoretically and empirical Bayes performance is reported on priors calibrated from over four thousand internet experiments.

source_observation.claim: The reported regret from empirical Bayes selection can decrease faster than the error involved in estimating the underlying prior.

interpretation.claim: Decision quality may require less statistical accuracy than full value estimation.

application.claim: When the operational goal is choosing high-value units rather than estimating every value precisely, evaluate decision regret directly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how these rates or conclusions change outside the stated asymptotic and prior assumptions.

unknowns: The parametric prior family and measurement-error assumptions are unspecified.
The regret definition, constants, and regularity conditions are unspecified.
The internet-experiment calibration procedure and empirical evaluation details are unspecified.
